rapport_notes: Jules was friendly, patient through pricing confusion, and professional throughout; no coldness or friction detected.
process_discipline_notes: No repeated differentiators across stages. However, after the pricing anchor/adjustment explanation, Jules did not hold silence — he continued immediately with clarification and pivot rather than letting the customer absorb.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: let's start with a few questions to get us in the right track this should take about six minutes or so and then I'll be able to build you an accurate quote
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Other than the price. Do you have any specific concerns or questions you want answers during this call today?
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Just the furniture. So we're not going to be moving any boxes. / No, I think we can handle the boxes. / Sounds good then. [No follow-up: 'what else is on your list' or 'tell me more about the furniture concern.']
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: usually for town homes, this size, it takes two movers, anywhere from five to seven hours to completely move. So for example, it took us, like an even five hour. The cost is $1,105 if it takes the seven hours, it's $1,505
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_estimate_is_a_window: So, you know what? Oh, sorry, go ahead. I was gonna say just to give you some ideas usually for town homes, this size, of course it would still depend on how much staff we're actually going to be moving on move day
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_beats_it_pay_less: for example, the move took about five hours and fifteen minutes. You'll only be charged until the fifteen minute mark. Not like for the whole hour.

top_strength: Jules nailed the quid pro quo framing upfront and delivered a solid pricing anchor with range personalization (5–7 hours for a 1300→1700 sqft townhome move), plus patiently walked the customer through confusing 15-minute proration math without losing them.
coaching_note: After 'Do you have any specific concerns,' Jules got 'just the furniture' but never asked 'what else is on your list' or 'tell me more about why furniture is the main concern' — he pivoted straight to logistics; go two layers deep on every concern raised, and close the call by locking the rate and asking 'would you like our help with your move' instead of handing off without an explicit ask.
